text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.76% today as oil prices steadied above $89 per barrel, following a sharp dip two days earlier when climate talks collapsed on November 23rd. That collapse—where governments rejected a U.N. draft deal that excluded fossil fuels—removed a near-term regulatory headwind, and the stock has recovered most of the 2.9% loss it took that day. The slight uptick suggests investors viewed the failed climate accord as a relief rather than a threat to near-term energy demand and company operations.

The broader context is mixed: geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Ukraine continue to create supply-side noise around refinery and production capacity, while energy prices remain range-bound. Oil's modest stability around $90 isn't strong enough to drive a meaningful rally, which is why the stock remains down 1.6% over two weeks despite today's recovery.
